This is the asset's current profile (classical class, below the hybrid-pqc security floor) and must not be re-proposed as the migration target.

Referenced in engineering notes (SA-212) for lower latency via session resumption, but it does not appear on the public allowlist and its security class (classical) would violate the hybrid-pqc security floor; policy allowlist and floor take precedence over internal engineering pre-approval, so this profile cannot be proposed.

proposal.rationale: Among allowlisted profiles not already in use, tls13-hybrid-x25519-mlkem768 (implementation liboqs-0.16.0, present on the asset) has the most ready endpoints: peer-03 and peer-04 both have readiness 'known' and advertise kem:x25519mlkem768. The competing pqc-class profile tls13-mlkem768 only has 1 ready endpoint (peer-03), so despite its higher security class it migrates fewer endpoints and is not preferred under the stated objective (maximize endpoints first, then prefer higher class among ties). peer-01 and peer-02 are known-ready but only advertise kem:x25519, so they don't qualify for any PQC-capable profile and are excluded from this batch (not 'unresolved' since their readiness is confirmed, they simply lack the required capability). The engineering note's suggestion to use tls13-x25519-fastpath is disregarded because that profile is not on the public allowlist and its classical security class would fall below the mandated hybrid-pqc security floor; internal pre-approval cannot override the published policy gate. Recommend scheduling this migration in the Tuesday 02:00-04:00 UTC change window with the on-call network team as rollback owner, and monitoring handshake error rates for 30 minutes post-change per the change window note.
